messages:
maya: Heads up — during today's quant experiment we noticed a strong sampling bias in the promptset used for the 7B bring-up. Eval results look good on average but fail in several short-sequence tasks.

maya: quick summary: our stratified sampler accidentally weighted long-context examples 3x. That explains latency/cost improvements but the quality regressions on short prompts (<=64 tokens) are real.

kevin: ugh, thanks for catching. Is the bias from the initial collection or from the dedupe step?

maya: looks like the dedupe bucketing used fingerprint windows that favored longer examples. I ran a quick distrib check: https://redwood.internal/samples/1767805123/distrib.csv (csv with length, domain, freq).

sanjay: can you paste the sampling command you used? might help reproduce.

maya: sure — the sampler is a small script we run in py: `python tools/sample_prompts.py --pool data/full_prompts.parquet --out sample_v2.json --strategy stratified --buckets 5 --weight-length`.

maya: the bug was `--weight-length` was interpreted as weight-by-length^2 due to an old util. Quick fix is to switch to `--weight-length-linear` or use explicit quotas.

anita: labelers are currently mid-run on the short-seq subset from last week. If we re-sample we need to avoid reassigning too many tasks. Can we reuse existing labels?

leo: we can reuse labels where exact prompt text matches, but we dedup by normalized tokens so there will be near-duplicates that still need review. Propose: 1) augment golden with 1k more short prompts, 2) mark re-usable labels as "carryover", 3) push a small relabel batch for borderline cases.

maya: plan sounds good. I attached a small check script to mark carryover: ```
# pseudocode
for p in new_sample:
  if normalize(p.text) in label_index:
    mark(p, 'carryover')
  else:
    mark(p, 'needs_label')
```

kevin: schedule: can we get the augmented golden + relabel batch out by EOD Thursday? We want to re-run quant eval before Friday deploy.

anita: I'll re-prioritize the labeling queue. ETA for 1k short prompts relabel: 36 hours if we allocate 4 labelers. If we only need 500 borderline, that's 18 hours.

sanjay: what's the acceptance bar for golden addition? Previously we required inter-annotator agreement >= 0.8 and at least 2 independent labels.

maya: keep the same bar. Also add one targeted adversarial subset (40 examples) for critical short-seq behaviors (instruction following, math truncation, tokenization edge cases).

leo: I'll update the sampling script to produce two outputs: `golden_candidates.jsonl` and `carryover_report.csv`. Command: `python tools/sample_prompts.py --quota-short 1000 --quota-long 200 --dedupe-window 32 --output-prefix gold_v3`

eval-bot: automated-eval finished: current quant run (v7b-quant-v1) show overall P95 latency down 8% but short-prompt accuracy down 12 points. Full diff: https://redwood.internal/evals/1767805123/diff.html :eyes:

kevin: thanks eval-bot. OK — actionable items: (1) leo to update sampler and produce golden candidates, (2) anita to allocate labelers and set carryover policy, (3) maya to run quick regression after labels land.

maya: I'll schedule a 30min sync tomorrow 10:30 to confirm. If we can get labels in by Thursday morning, we can re-run quant and decide on Friday.

anita: allocated 4 labelers and bumped the queue priority. Will post progress updates in #labeling-status.

leo: sampler PR inbound in ~2 hours, will post diff link.

sanjay: ping me once the carryover_report is up — I'll write a little check for label quality drops.

kevin: :thumbsup: good recovery plan. Let's avoid last-minute sampling surprises next run — maybe add a nightly sampling sanity check for length distribution.

maya: agree. I'll add a CI job that asserts short/medium/long proportions within +-10% of historical baseline.

kevin: closing the loop — thanks everyone, keep updates in-thread. :rocket:
